  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains how the supernal delight descends through the "innards" (angels) into physical pleasures, and how the souls of Israel refine the waste of this delight, leading to the revelation of the Ein Sof that encompasses all worlds in the World to Come.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">For behold, from the supernal delight, it fell into the Holy Shechinah and became physical delights.</t>
    <t s="2">And Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Akiva, when they saw a great city*35</t>
    <t s="3">of Rome, Rabban Gamliel wept, Rabbi Akiva laughed. Rabban Gamliel wept over the descent of the supernal delight that had descended so low,</t>
    <t s="4">and Rabbi Akiva laughed: if for those who transgress His will it is so, for those who do His will, all the more so.</t>
    <t s="5">And it is the waste of the supernal delight, and as it is said, "And all my innards [praise] Your holy name," for there are angels*36</t>
    <t s="6">called "innards" that refine the influx.</t>
    <t s="7">And just as the innards refine the food, where the choice part becomes vitality for the brain and heart, and the waste is expelled outward,</t>
    <t s="8">so too the angels called "innards" refine the influx, so that the waste is expelled outward and becomes physical delights.</t>
    <t s="9">And likewise, the elevations from below are also refined, whatever can ascend, etc. And this is the matter of "angels of God ascending and descending" on the ladder, in Torah and prayer, as explained elsewhere.*37</t>
    <t s="10">And the souls of Israel below refine the waste of the supernal delight,</t>
    <t s="11">for this is the descent of souls below—to refine the physical delights so that they become included in Divinity, and through this, an advantage of light is made, for the advantage of light is from the darkness, whereby there shines the revelation of the aspect of the Ein Sof that encompasses all worlds.</t>
    <t s="12">This is the entire difference between the Garden of Eden and the World to Come.</t>
    <t s="13">For the revelation of the Garden of Eden is from the aspect of the One who fills all worlds, and therefore there are distinctions of levels, as is known, for the One who fills all worlds is an aspect of division, etc. And because the light of the One who fills all worlds shines in revelation and in a revelation of essence,</t>
    <t s="14">this is a wondrous delight indeed, and it is better that I be judged*38</t>
    <t s="15">and come to the World to Come, for all the sufferings of Gehinnom are worthwhile, and it is known*39</t>
    <t s="16">that the sufferings of Iyov for seventy years are not comparable to the sufferings of Gehinnom for one hour,</t>
    <t s="17">yet all the sufferings of Gehinnom are worthwhile even for a glimpse of the Torah, and certainly for a glimpse of the Garden of Eden, because it is a delight beyond measure.</t>
    <t s="18">Nevertheless, this is a revelation of the aspect of the One who fills all worlds.</t>
    <t s="19">Therefore, the revelation is only for souls without bodies,</t>
    <t s="20">because the One who fills all worlds is an aspect of light in a vessel,</t>
    <t s="21">and the vessel must be according to the measure of the light,</t>
    <t s="22">and although according to the manner of the vessel is the manner of the light,</t>
    <t s="23">or according to the manner of the light and revelation is the coming into being of the vessel's existence,</t>
    <t s="24">for in truth both are true, as explained elsewhere,*40</t>
    <t s="25">nevertheless, however it may be, the vessel must be fit to receive the light, and the body is not a vessel for the revelation of the light of the One who fills all worlds,</t>
    <t s="26">and therefore the revelation is for souls without bodies.</t>
    <t s="27">But the World to Come is a revelation of the aspect of the One who encompasses all worlds, where there is no division of levels, therefore it is only one level,</t>
    <t s="28">and although each one is singed by the canopy of his fellow, this is because even in the encompassing lights there are particular encompassing lights,</t>
    <t s="29">nevertheless, it is all one level.</t>
    <t s="30">And it is known that in the One who fills all worlds there is a division of higher and lower, which are divided in their level and in their essential superiority, and this is that in the Garden of Eden there is an upper and a lower,</t>
    <t s="31">but not so the aspect of the One who encompasses all worlds; although there are particular encompassing lights,</t>
    <t s="32">nevertheless, in their essential essence, it is one essence, as explained elsewhere.</t>
    <t s="33">And the revelation of the World to Come will be specifically for souls in bodies, because their beginning is wedged in their end specifically, for the end of action arose in thought first, for the ultimate intention is in the existence of the yesh (somethingness), that the yesh be nullified to the Ayin (nothingness),</t>
    <t s="34">and therefore physical yesh has a connection to the aspect of the One who encompasses all worlds, as explained elsewhere in the explanation that they will bring a royal garment,</t>
    <t s="35">and therefore the revelation of the future will be specifically below, for souls in bodies,</t>
    <t s="36">and on the contrary, the primary revelation will be to the body, and the soul will receive through the body, as explained at length in the discourse "Eileh Toldot Noach" (p. 237).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the two "Ani" (I am) aspects—the encompassing and filling—and how the work of refinement now prepares for the future revelation, illustrated by the different perceptions of Seraphim and Ofanim.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "I, I am He"—two times "Ani." This is the matter of "I am first" and "I am last." "I am first" is the aspect of the One who encompasses all worlds, and "I am last" is the aspect of the One who fills all worlds.</t>
    <t s="2">And now, there is one "Ani," the aspect of the One who fills all worlds,</t>
    <t s="3">and in the future there will be two times "Ani," meaning the revelation of the aspect of the One who encompasses all worlds,</t>
    <t s="4">and there will be a union of the two times "Ani," meaning that there will be a revelation of the aspect of the One who encompasses all worlds in the aspect of the end of action, the aspect of Malchut,</t>
    <t s="5">and it says "See now," meaning that the preparation for this is now, for through the work now in the matter of refinements, through this, in the future, "I, I am He" will be.</t>
    <t s="6">And this will be understood from the matter of Seraphim and Ofanim.*41</t>
    <t s="7">For the Seraphim say "Kadosh" (Holy), for they perceive how the Ein Sof is holy and separate. For the Seraphim are in the world of Beriah, where Imma Ila'ah nests in the Throne, therefore they perceive their vitality—how it is merely an illumination, and how the Ein Sof is holy and separate from the worlds.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is "Seraphim stand above Him" for the Name Ado-nai, because they perceive their vitality, as explained in Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah, Part 1, Chapter 5, regarding the matter of the laws of the Torah, which is in the aspect of makif (encompassing) and mukaf (encompassed), for when one perceives the matter of the law, he encompasses it,</t>
    <t s="9">even though the matter of the law is the wisdom of the Torah, which is infinitely higher than his intellect,</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless, his intellect encompasses it when he perceives it.</t>
    <t s="11">And likewise with the Seraphim, because they perceive*42</t>
    <t s="12">their vitality, they stand above Him,</t>
    <t s="13">and the Ofanim and the Holy Chayot are in great tumult due to the lack of perception,</t>
    <t s="14">for the Chayot are in Yetzirah, where there is the beginning of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, which conceals and hides, so that they do not have perception of the aspect of "Kadosh,"</t>
    <t s="15">and all the more so the Ofanim in Asiyah, where the concealment and distance are greater, as it is written, "And behold, one ofan (wheel)*43</t>
    <t s="16">on the earth," and the Targum translates it as "from below," as explained in Likkutei Torah in the discourse "Haazinu,"</t>
    <t s="17">and from this comes their tumult,</t>
    <t s="18">and through the tumult they draw from a higher level, which is the matter of "Blessed be the glory of God from His place," and in the manner of "from His place He is inclined,"*44</t>
    <t s="19">for they draw the aspect of the glory of God from its root and source. And all the more so the delights below, which conceal and hide the most, for they conceal the Divine intention within them, since in every thing there is a Divine intention,</t>
    <t s="20">and the physical conceals this, and moreover, the totality of the concealment that conceals Divinity, and from this comes a very great tumult,</t>
    <t s="21">meaning that it is very distressing to him that he is in such a world, where the influx comes through many concealments and veils,</t>
    <t s="22">and likewise in himself, in particular, that he is in a state where his influx must specifically come through intermediaries that conceal, and also that he greatly desires that nevertheless it should not conceal and hide from him, and that he be given over and devoted to matters of Divinity, and that in every thing there be a Divine intention, and through this an advantage of light is made. And as in teshuvah (repentance), a baal teshuvah draws upon himself a greater power, for in the place where baalei teshuvah stand, completely righteous individuals cannot stand, and this is because it comes from the distance, which awakens in the innermost part of his soul.</t>
    <t s="23">And likewise is the tumult that comes through concealment and distance, for the tumult is greater, and "tumult" (רעש) has the letters of "gate" (שער), the aspect of "This is the gate to God,"</t>
    <t s="24">for there is a gate on the right and a gate on the left.*45</t>
    <t s="25">The gate on the right is the matter of "This is the gate to God,"</t>
    <t s="26">the gate on the left is the aspect of hairs (שערות), which is an external drawing,</t>
    <t s="27">and just as the hairs, although they draw from the brain,</t>
    <t s="28">their vitality is very constricted, due to the interruption of the skull bone,</t>
    <t s="29">and therefore when one cuts the hairs, he does not feel pain.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the allegory of the "curls" as mounds of halachic laws, and how through the negation of partnership with physical things, one draws the revelation of the aspect of the Singular One in the future.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And the allegory for this is what is said, "His locks are curls"*46</t>
    <t s="2">—these are mounds upon mounds of halachot,</t>
    <t s="3">for through curling the hairs to separate the halachot so that they do not contradict each other,</t>
    <t s="4">behold, "Curl it and it will exalt you," for the soul is exalted through this to the aspect of "the hair of His head like clean wool," as explained in Likkutei Torah in the discourse "Ki Bayom Hazeh Yechaper" (the second).</t>
    <t s="5">Nevertheless, all this is only the aspect of hairs,</t>
    <t s="6">for "the Torah emanates from Chochmah," and the illumination of delight in Chochmah is through the Mazalot and hairs, for Abba draws from the Mazal of "Notzer" (the eighth). But the gate on the right is a wide gate,</t>
    <t s="7">and it is like the matter of "He answered me with a broad [space of] Yah," in the aspect of the essential breadth of the Ein Sof,</t>
    <t s="8">meaning that through "From the straits I called out," through this "He answered me with a broad [space of] Yah."</t>
    <t s="9">And likewise, in the aspect of the tumult that comes from the concealments of physical things,</t>
    <t s="10">when one performs a mitzvah with them, such as tzitzit with physical wool, tefillin with physical parchment, shofar with the physical horn of a ram, sukkah with physical roofing, the four species in the lulav with physical plants, etc.,</t>
    <t s="11">behold, "Your mitzvah is exceedingly broad," for they become broad vessels to receive the aspect of the supernal "exceedingly," which is without limit.</t>
    <t s="12">And likewise, through the negation of partnership (shituf), meaning that even when engaged in physical things, he does not consider them at all, and he is devoted only to Divinity, and through this he makes an advantage of light, etc. And just as a person*47</t>
    <t s="13">does not see from the white of the eye but from the black of it, so too the advantage of light is specifically from the darkness. For through the work now, the revelation in the future will be the aspect of the Essence of the Ein Sof, blessed be He. And this is what is said in the Midrash Rabbah: "But in the future, I alone." And it can be said that this is like the matter of "You are He, God, alone," the aspect of "He" and "Havayah" as it is in the aspect of "alone."</t>
    <t s="14">And the matter is that through the refinements of Tohu alone, by which one inherits the aspect of the lights of Tohu, there is also drawn from the aspect of the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above the aspect of Tohu and Tikkun,</t>
    <t s="15">for the construction of Tohu was in order to destroy,</t>
    <t s="16">and the breaking of Tohu was in order to build. Therefore, through the refinement of Tikkun, there is drawn from the aspect of the Ein Sof that is above Tohu and Tikkun, for in the first root is the aspect of "alone," and in the future it will be "I alone." And this is also the matter of "I, I am He, and there is no god with Me," for there is no partner with Me, meaning the aspect of the Singular One, the aspect of "One and not in number,"</t>
    <t s="17">and it is through the negation of the matter of partnership below, through this there will be in the future a revelation of the aspect of the Singular One. And this is "You have made Me a single entity in the world," "God is One," to exclude the matter of idolatry, which is complete separation,</t>
    <t s="18">and also to exclude the matter of partnership (shituf), meaning "there is no god with Me." And below, this means that one should not think that physical things are the source of livelihood, for that is complete separation, God forbid,</t>
    <t s="19">but also this: that he should not consider them as anything at all</t>
    <t s="20">(and it can be said that the sign of this is the matter of equanimity, that yes and no are equal).</t>
    <t s="21">And this is the negation of partnership, and through this one draws the revelation of the aspect of "One" below, the aspect of "You are One."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
